headline: Congress cancels a consumer bureau rule that would have let it supervise large nonbank payment app companies.
what_it_does: This law cancels a rule issued by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) on December 10, 2024. That rule would have put large payment app companies that are not banks under CFPB supervision. It covered companies handling at least 50 million transactions a year that are not small businesses. With the rule canceled, the CFPB does not gain this supervision power under it.

who_it_affects.group: Large nonbank companies that run digital payment apps
who_it_affects.how: They will not be subject to CFPB supervision, such as exams, under this rule.

who_it_affects.group: People who use payment apps to send money or pay for things
who_it_affects.how: The apps they use will not be supervised by the CFPB under this rule.
The bureau loses the supervision authority the rule would have given it over these companies.

when_it_takes_effect: May 9, 2025, when it was signed into law.
